#81370 7 2005-07-06T03:32:37Z Red Reamer
Well being a up and coming philosopher, heres my take on sanity.

Sanity, as it is often defined, is the condition in which one is considered mentally sound. This stems questions relating to what is mentality, and of course, what is healthy? Many believe that the human mind is subjugated into several distinctive sections; the sensual, affection, moral, intellectual, and spiritual elements. In every department there exists a power that rules the predispositions of the mind, which we know as reason. To maintain sanity through reason, two things are required. First, the harmonious working of all the elements of mind, and second, the ability to analyse and differentiate between the separate components. It can thus be argued that sanity is an equal development of all mans mental faculties. Wherever one or other is deficient, there is insanity, or unsoundness. Though it may not be immediately apparent, unless it manifests itself in some extreme.


Sanity is also commonly recognized as the capacity to anticipate and appraise the effect of one's actions. And again this too raises similar doubts concerning the definition of reality and responsibility, for to anticipate one must be aware of ones surroundings and be able to somewhat accurately predict, and assess an outcome. It is often argued that whether or not reality is real, or whether it is in fact, a dream or delusion, a sane man believes that the world around him and the people in it are real. Thus reality is not a constant as such, but is relevant to the time at hand. Again, this affects responsibility, in that no sane man starts burning London in the belief that his servant will soon wake him for breakfast. The fact that, at any given moment, there is no completely tangible evidence that I am not in a dream is immaterial [to a sane person].

Further, responsibility can also be explained through practicality. A sane man believes that this world not only exists, but also matters. Therefore sanity leads a man to believe that there is an obligation upon us to interest ourselves in this vision or panorama of life.

And sane men believe that there is such a thing as a self, or ego, which is continuous. Thus responsibility and reality are concurrent in us, and cannot be disposed of without disposing of oneself, which under the terms of the previous supposition is undesirable.

Thus it can be argued that most sane men believe, that they have a power of choice and responsibility for action.

There is also another possibility relating to perception. It is possible that the sane perceive what is actually there. Their sensations are attuned to reality. The insane however, do not perceive the same reality, nor perhaps, do they express their experiences or thoughts in the same format. Thus for some, madness is not a sickness, but simply a misplacement. There are obviously numerous counter-arguments against this, and it seems impossible to prove or disprove the theory, unlikely though it may be.

Sanity can also be described as the dedication to discovering and acting according to a principle of discoverable truth. This has no repercussions, such as the last two definitions, in that there is no mention of responsibility or reality, as such. This separates conscience from reason, and simply states that to be considered sane, ones actions must be based upon something that is ultimately regarded as true. And so another uncertainty arises; What is truth? Truth can be defined as the correspondence of a pictorial or symbolic representation to the thing being represented. Thus the question can be reworded as What is it that is said to be true? And so a circle is formed in that the subject must rationalize their true value in order to be considered sane, yet must arguably be considered sane to rationalize.

Another issue, concerning sanity involves the question of rationality, and logistics. Is it possible to be insane, and yet still form rational arguments? Some might think so, though many definitions of sanity (and thus insanity, being the opposite) preclude such an act. If we cannot for see consequences, or do not perceive what is considered reality, or even do not base our actions on a fact of life, then logical thought is impossible. There is also the possibility that insanity is simply an emotional state, in which case rationality is entirely possible, just unlikely.

In conclusion, no matter what you think sanity is, for the most part, sanity is a comparative measure, which is designed to separate the socially unfit from functional members of society. In day-to-day life, this explanation will suffice. Whilst people are incapable of being unswervingly rational, they can be considered sane by comparison to those who are completely inept at rationalisation.

Fun 15 Points: Well, being slightly noobish in skill, this tested me, but I did eventually get it. Again, frustrating, but satisfying, just like many of the in game levels; 13/15

Total: 35/40

The idea of this is, and whether or not anyone else does it, is that I will update this thread with my new maps. I know this could be seen as an attempt to blow my own horn and raise my post count, but really I just want people to look at, and mainly comment on my maps.

Heres the jyst of it. I make a new map (or maybe mroe than one on a slow day) every day pretty much. I will update this thread when I make a new one. I don't expect everyone to look at it, or rate, but that is obviously the idea, so please do. I will no longer spam maps on the IRC channel as well, so you guys are safe
The other reason I'm doing this is because often I post a comment and the person it is aimed at never comes back, making the whole system quite redundant.

I will never double post. I will edit if no one has posted since my last one. And for anyone that posts in here (and has actually made the effort to look at my map(s)), I will look at their most recent work, and unrated stuff. So it's kinda like a map-rating thread, and atramentis' thread, plus "My Maps" on numa, all rolled in to one.

And finally (for now) Jenga
One of my best yet I reckon.

Whew, tommorow, or the day after, there will be another largish update with three maps (theres two in the queue right now). And by all means, tell me if they suck.

#102661 269 2005-09-22T01:05:54Z Red Reamer
I thought I'd check back, as this topic as progressed so much since I "left."

And I like where this has gone. I can now see my problem with religion, it is based on a few base points, that I cannot accept, despite the reasoning and faith of others.

1. That there is meaning in life. I don't see it. I'm not just being a depressed teen, I just can't beleive that there is an ultimate purpose. Or, if there is, I cannot believe that we experience it straight after death, and that repenting our sins is enough to get us there. The universe, the planet, life itself is a big scale thing. One life, is not a huge factor. Maybe there will be a "Big Suck," at the end of time, and then perhaps, a form of afterlife exists, and one should worry about God. But that is certainly a long way off, and so far beyond the control of man, that it may as well not exist.

2. That "bad" people deserve second chances, and compassion I do not think that my take on evil and religions are too well alligned. If you repent later, if you do something in the name of the Lord, if you beleive it is right, then bad acts are suddenly acceptable again. Society, the justice system, our minds are not built like this. Hitler thought he was doing the right thing, was religious and was still obviously a raving loon. The context, the reasoning and the motivation all need to be looked at to acess an act. Religion does not entirely do this, they say, yes it was wrong, but now you know that, repent and all is forgiven.

3. That the supernatural is the work of God Jesus was some guy with new gifts. Maybe he just had some awesome herbs he gave people. Yet christianity works him in, deservingly or not. Joan of Arc heard voices. Obviously it was God talking to her. Obviously. The great flood? It was probably just that, a big friggen flood. So add Noah, some nonsense and God, and hey presto, a biblical tale. I think that rather than explaining things, religion makes it a moving story of hardship, and lectures people on it. TDL is right in this aspect, if you believe in a greater meaning in life, then religion might be the gate to it. But religion is by no means a path to greater understanding of history/physics and the like, because to a large extent, it just ignores such topics.

4. That God is good. I'm with TDL again, assume that the rest is flawed (which it entirely possible/probable), why should we worship this guy? Because he created us? Think about it, if we are created in his image, then is he not as depraved as us? I cannot see him as being perfect in any way, he is vengful, petty and overbearing. If a being of that power exists, why should he care what we do? I think that there are better things to do than worship a being that has had very little input in our lifes, for quite some time. By that I mean, why was he so prominent in the bible, yet today, there has been no contact for 2000 years?

You might also notice that if I believe point one, than the following points are rather pointless (heheh). I'm making these points for arguements sake; suppose that I'm proven wrong about a, then problem b still remains.

And now I conclude my ramblings, and feel much better for it. In most cases I did not get my point across as well as I would have liked to, but what the hey. It is a start. My problem these days is less with religion and God, but with religious people, and their stance on life.

Quote: http://www.visualnation.com/interesting/macsbetter.html
1.) Mac is well-connected: you can daisy chain up to seven SCSI devices internally or externally to the Mac. The typical Wintel machine does not include a port for connecting external devices. Rather, PCs have an IDE interface that only allows you to hook up two internal hard drives. You have to buy a SCSI card to hook up external devices or buy a drive to hook up to the PC's external (and deadly slow) parallel port.

2.) DOS is a pain: No matter what PC users say, Windows 95 still has DOS lurking in the shadows. Try using a question mark, a slash, or various non-letters in your filename-you'll get all kinds of weird error messages. And if you have problems at start-up, like a PC card is missing and your system expects it to be there, you'll drop immediately into DOS.

3.) 32-Character Filenames: Even though Windows 95 allows for 32-character filenames, just try opening that file on an older PC. This makes filesharing nearly impossible between Windows 95 machines and Windows 3.1. All versions of Mac OS understand 32 character file names.

4.) Mac is easier to set up: A 10-year-old Mac user was pitted against the Editor-in-Chief of a major PC magazine in a contest at a recent Software Publishers Association meeting to see which platform was easiest to set up. The 10-year-old took 16 minutes, 15 seconds to get his Mac system up and running, while the Wintel expert clocked in at 26 minutes, 15 seconds.

5.) Wintel machines are more prone to viruses: More than 8,000 viruses exist for the PC, with 100 to 200 new bugs introduced each month. The Mac has only succumbed to 40 or 50 viruses in its history.

6.) Macs are faster: With many Windows applications still in 16-bit mode, the 32-bit applications and RISC processors of the Mac leave Wintel machines in the dust.

7.) Quicktime, an Apple product: The standard in the Mac industry for video file formats is widely used by Windows because it is cross-platform and easy to use. Furthermore, Quicktime is integrated into the MacOS and so all of its features can be incorporated into applications and the internet.

8.) Macs are the choice for internet users: Even though in the total desktop market Apple only holds 8% of the market, on the internet 25% of the computers are Macintosh. Apple Internet Servers are used widely on the internet and a large percent of web pages on the web were created on Apples.

9.) Macintosh leads in graphics and color: Unless you are only doing word processing, the Mac is the best computer for graphic design and color work. Desktop publishing was created on the Mac with the advent of PostScript, PageMaker, and the LaserWriter. Even art departments of PC magazines like PC Computing, PC Magazine, and PC World use Macs exclusively.

10.) Mac is truly plug-and-play: Even though Windows 95 is supposed to be plug-and-play, the truth is that it isn't that simple. With a Mac you just install the hardware, click on the installer, and you are ready to go. With Windows 95, if you want to make any changes in the configuration, you could spend hours with technical support trying to override the closed Windows 95 system.

#5307 1 2005-11-21T13:47:03Z Red Reamer
The office window stood ajar, letting the cold, high altitude wind stream through the executive office. It trickled through the blinds, which bounced and shook in playful mimicry of the shaking, huddled form amongst them. Johnson sat near the edge of the window, facing slightly away from it, as though this slim angle would lessen the menace of a seven-story drop. The wind buffeted around him, at times making him rock and sway dangerously close to the edge, but he seemed oblivious to his surroundings as he hugged his knees. Stray documents floated on the breeze, littering the office with trivialities.

The door burst open, a stunned individual in the doorway. He slowly took in the situation; paper floated past, a chair lay sprawled on the ground, recently overturned and Johnson, a colleague of years past, cowered near the gaping window. Spotting the hunched figure, the intruder became more distressed. He leaned back into the hallway, searching both directions for any sign of help. Finding none, he swallowed hard and finally let go of the door handle. As he prepared to enter further into the office, a voice rang out, “Fuck off Davis.” There was no malice in the voice; it was a level, clear statement. For a moment, Davis seemed to be considering Johnson’s advice, and then again realised the severity of the situation. The wind fluttered his tie, and it danced upon his chest.

They remained frozen for several minutes; Johnson completely apathetic of his visitor, and Davis overwhelmed, and at somewhat of a loss as to his next move. Davis edged carefully inside, and slowly closed the door. After this decisive action, he again lost his nerve, and stood, silently shuffling near the door. Johnson at last noticed him and looked around. He spared Davis a look of mild contempt, and then returned his attention to his feet and the nearby abyss. “Johnson?” ventured Davis warily. Receiving no answer, he took two steps forward, and tried again, with a little more insistence, “Johnson?!”

Johnson, resigned to his friend’s persistence, slowly span around, so that his back faced the opening. Having gotten Johnson’s attention, Davis was once more unsettled. The usual conversation starters seemed clumsy in this context. Noticing his co-workers impatience, he settled on “The very first bomb dropped by the Allies on Berlin during World War II killed the only elephant in the Berlin Zoo.” Davis gave this a moment to sink in, as Johnson raised an eyebrow, entirely taken aback by this statement. Finally, unable to withhold his curiosity, he asked, “And how does that relate to our given situation?” Again, Davis, who seemed much more at ease and in control of the situation, paused. Then said, “What you’re contemplating seems almost as pointless.”

Several more minutes past, as Davis marvelled at his own genius, smiling softly. Johnson let his head rest on his knees, warily eying his associate, also impressed with what had been said. He spoke, still with flat intonation, “Quite an assumption you made there.” Davis, who had been staring out the window, his eyes following a stray letter that had wafted outside and now fluttered lazily downwards, snapped his attention back to Johnson. He continued smiling, obviously pleased to have broken the ice and said rather jovially, “Well it wasn’t that far a jump, seeing you crouched by the window.” Johnson nodded slowly, though perhaps not to this comment, but to an unspoken idea that just now ran through his thoughts.

“I did not mean your rationale that I intend to kill myself, I referred to your assumption that death is pointless,” Johnson replied. This remark shattered Davis’s sense of satisfaction, and the smile left his face, replaced with a thoughtful frown. “But where are my manners, please, have a seat,” continued Johnson. Again, Davis appeared discouraged; an impression that was heightened when he again noticed that the only chair was upturned. Realising that Johnson was waiting for him to seat himself, he hurriedly moved towards the chair, clumsily righting it. Wheeling it over, he sat, and gazed at his companion. More time passed, as Davis carefully chose his words, feeling that another astute observation was expected.

Johnson remained motionless, prepared to allow his guest all the time needed in which to respond. Abruptly, Davis broke the silence, “How can taking your own life be anything other than pointless?” He seemed concerned, and the frown had not left his face. He peered intently at Johnson, as sweat trickled from his brow. Davis’s obvious agitation amused his host.

Johnson shrugged, in no hurry to provide an answer. His steely calm was off-putting, given the gravity of the situation. Davis had expected outrage or depression, and having received only nonchalance, was confused and nervous. A car alarm pierced the silence, drifting upwards from the street below. Johnson appeared to return to the present, and smiled absentmindedly at Davis.

“My friend, my life is all but finished anyway.” Johnson voiced. Davis did not like this verbal dance, which continued to dodge the issue at hand. He did not want to continue this farce any longer.

“How can you know that from this side of death?” Davis asked, almost angrily. This resentment put Johnson off balance for the first time. He didn’t seem to understand the fervour in his guest’s tone. Johnson narrowed his eyes, as they flickered over Davis’s face, searching for an explanation.

“I don’t expect you to understand, nor did I expect you to care.” Johnson said quite candidly. Davis again felt the awkwardness of the situation, and shifted uneasily in his seat. Johnson smiled. A grin that voiced an understanding known only to Johnson; it spoke of truths uncovered and the satisfaction gained thereafter. He rose suddenly, and Davis followed suit.

“Do not think ill of me.” Johnson said, putting particular emphasis on the last words he would ever speak.

He raised his arms like wings, and fell backwards, into the void. A soft thud drifted up, as Davis rushed to the window. A crowd gathered below, eager to partake in the spectacle. Davis staggered back to the door and hurried out, no longer comfortable in the dead man’s office. The wind blew the door shut, producing a dull sound that echoed, reminiscent of its owner’s recent demise.

© Nick [Kashkin] 2005

#6180 1 2006-01-12T13:04:31Z Red Reamer
This is actually an idea from a Kurt Vonnegut novel - The Sirens of Titan.
Basically, the religion is based around the idea that fate is non-existant, and that luck is unrelated to God, or His will. Other than that of course is the main point, which is that God has no influence upon our lives, nor does he appear to care about humanity as a whole, or in specific cases. The religion strives for equality and peace through spiritual guidance, but not through worship. It claims that God is apart from our lives, neither present nor omnipresent; detached and disinterested.

Information on the book is available through Wiki - here.
I would reccomend reading the book for a better understanding. Apart from the religion, it's a good read.

Anyway, I wanted to gauge people's opinions. Is this, do you suppose, a valid basis for a religion?

After Sal has made his opinion known, and Hailey and Tequila have assured him of their interest, I put forth my thoughts on the matter.

"There is a reason that we are all bound for Westreach, but that reason is only known to the whigged gentlemen who passed on the map. #245657 6 2006-10-25T05:54:15Z Red Reamer
I think mine takes the cake.

Our Modern World History teacher sets two assignments, right? One's an essay on Germany's fallibility in WWI, and the other is on the cause of the war in relation to the assasination of Franz Ferdinand. A friend goes to hand up one of the essays (I can't remember which was which), and finds that the second page of a two page essay is missing. He tells our teacher that he'll print him another copy later in the day, and does so. So he's handed up two pages of the same essay at different times.

Our teacher, being the genius that he is, obviously doesn't remember this sequence of events. He marks each page as though they were seperate essays! And my friend got a 12/20 and a 9/20! So this teacher gave him 9/20 for half a page on a different topic (though related). My friend of course, argued that he should get 21/20 for the piece, and was shot down. Two weeks later he hands up the second essay, convincing our teacher that he had handed it up, and it had somehow been lost...

This same teacher failed to notice that a friend of ours would sporadically join the class, just for the hell of it. He never handed anything up, wasn't on the role, didn't do a test, and it took a semester for him to be noticed. At which point, our teacher acted as though he had known all along (we knew he hadn't, he overhead us paying him out for not noticing the day before) and playfully reprimanded us.

Oh, and we did one test all year. Guess what our end of year exam was? Basically the same test. In a different order...

And at this point, I went to a private school. Heheh, fond memories though. Fond memories...

The signature makers have banded together, in one thread, and now offer sigs to those who want them. If anyone wants a sig, ask, using the format below. Then, one of the team will make it for you. Hell, you might even get more than one.

The format:
Quote: Sig Request
Primary colours:
Theme:
Renders/images:
Text:
Complexity:
Matching avatar (yes or no):
Dimensions (size):
Preferred artist (optional):
(Just a note, on the preferred artist part; I'd really hope that it is a rarely used option. In fact, I wasn't going to include it, but hopefully the (optional) qualifier dissuades people from constantly opting for a particular artist. Unless you have a really good reason, please don't ask.)

Important! To prevent favouritism or any other biases, this thread works on a first come first served basis. This post will be edited and updated to include the requests that have and haven't been made. #252523 3 2006-11-10T11:55:06Z Red Reamer
I think the often the most frustrating aspect of any romantic venture is that it by definition, is not strictly logical. I've been through similar stages where I tried to reason out my feelings, or interactions. Though we're pretty much the same age, and given that I'm unemotional to a fault, don't think I'm preaching, but given my experiences, I'd say it is best just to let things happen. In any first love, you'll probably find you antagonize over things more than is prudent - which is only natural - but it's important not to get too caught up in rationalizing, or self-questioning.

Now that I've said that, I'll accept that it's almost impossible. Especially as, to an extent, I can appreciate your desire and drive to be in a relationship. I guess though, seeing how disastrously mine turned out after I "forced" it, that this sort of need isn't the best precursor for love. Though again, that might just be me. I dunno man, I got through this stage, but I wouldn't recommend my methodology. Hell, do the opposite of what I did, that might work. The sibling pressure sucks, which I would know nothing about but can still sort of appreciate (friends, cousins etc.).

All I can really say is, and this ties on from my "do-the-opposite-to-Nick" stratagem, is that loneliness breeds loneliness. Whether or not your friends' company entirely satisfies you or not, get amongst them. Also, I'd avoid bleeding this sort of worry on a regular basis. And, assuming I did everything wrong (which is quite probable), things may turn out fine. As far as girl advice goes, I'm not even going to offer any; it's too personal, and vague from this vantage.

Catch me on MSN some time, if you feel like it. Oh and with regard to your supernatural, pre-dawn insanity, I think it's nothing to worry about. I entertained the idea that I was schizophrenic, for a time. Everyone has odd moments, whether they're self-created or a result of circumstance.

Anyway, rambling is good for the soul, I say.
Catch you later,
Nick.

#13707 1 2007-01-26T04:29:10Z Red Reamer


It's here. A little later than I promised, but we can all take solace in blaming Clovic. The mappers involved, and in fact, many that were not, know that the organisation of this pack was ... nightmarish. I cannot even remember when this enterprise began. However, we got here in the end. Thanks to all for sticking by me.

The title of this pack, auri sacra fames (ASF for short), is Latin, and translates as "accursed hunger for gold." I thought it appropriate - and Latin, thus, sexy.

Aju, astheoceanblue, Barabajagal, Clovic, spect and I are the main contributers; spect may only have made five maps, but I enjoyed them every bit as much as the others. He was also one of the first people I asked to work on this with me. Incidentally, this is the second level pack he has been involved in, a detail I was incorrect about during my Nterview.

There are also ten guest maps, made by maestro, rennaT, LittleViking001 and Sweep.

As mentioned, this pack is non-episodic, so I'd recommend playing them alphabetically. Feedback and demos (especially an all-gold for Crotch Pheasant) would be much appreciated. Enjoy.

Hell, he might even have. Either way; not a big deal.

N+ is awesome.

Very clean and snazzy new look. I just finished "Master Control". It's nice to be able to mash A after dying, rather than the spacebar. It's weird seeing people high-score my map. Very cool, though.

At any rate, thank you M&R, and can someone with talent please play some co-op with me?
